statement: Let n = len(arr). Call an integer sequence b (i.e., b[0],...,b[n-1] are integers) of length n an arr-feasible final array if there is a permutation p of the index set {0,...,n-1} such that: (i) for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= b[i] <= arr[p(i)]; (ii) b[0] = 1; and (iii) for every i with 1 <= i < n, |b[i] - b[i-1]| <= 1. The function returns Ok r, and r is the maximum of max_{0 <= j < n} b[j] over all arr-feasible final arrays b. Equivalently, r is the largest value that can occur in an integer array obtained from arr by any allowed sequence of rearrangements and decreases while satisfying the two required conditions.
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies the problem constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000000.
